findings.claim: Switching `buckets` from `Map` to `WeakMap` drops `size`, `clear()`, `forEach()` and iteration; any existing code in this module that inspects or resets the bucket map will break.
findings.rationale: `WeakMap` is not a structural superset of `Map`. Memoizer implementations commonly do `state.buckets.clear()` at the end of a parse, read `.size`, or iterate buckets to flush pending issues. I cannot see the rest of the file, so this is a suspicion rather than a confirmed break, but it is the most likely fallout of this type change and deserves verification.

findings.claim: Making the per-node bucket weak allows memo entries to be garbage collected mid-parse, so memoization becomes non-deterministic; an `Entry` whose `issues` is still `null` (children not yet parsed) can disappear if the only strong reference to its key object was the map itself.
findings.rationale: With a strong `Map` the entry was guaranteed to survive the whole parse. With a `WeakMap` the entry's lifetime is tied to the key object's reachability. If keys are transient wrapper/marker objects created per visit rather than caller-owned data, a GC-triggered miss changes behavior (recomputation, duplicated issues, or an undetected cycle). Moderate confidence: safe only if every key stays strongly reachable for the whole parse.

findings.claim: The new comment states the bucket is cached on the schema instance and "outlives the parse", which means memo entries keyed by a data object are now reused across separate parse calls with different contexts.
findings.rationale: An `Entry` carries `issues` produced under one parse's context (error map, path prefix, config). If the same object graph is parsed twice against the same schema, a cross-parse memo hit could return issues computed under the previous context. The strong `Map` was presumably per-parse state, so this is a behavior change callers could be surprised by. Confidence moderate — depends on how `attach` scopes the bucket, which is not visible in this hunk.

findings.claim: `backEdges` as a `WeakSet` can no longer be iterated, sized, or cleared, and its membership can silently shrink under GC.
findings.rationale: Back-edge tracking usually needs a drain/clear step once a cycle resolves (e.g., walking recorded nodes to propagate issues). `WeakSet` supports only `add`/`has`/`delete`, so such logic breaks. A node dropped by GC would also silently stop being reported as a back-edge. Same caveat: consuming code is not visible here.

findings.claim: `WeakMap`/`WeakSet` throw `TypeError` on non-object keys, whereas `Map`/`Set` accepted anything; if any key reaching this state is a primitive (or a registered symbol) at runtime, the memoizer now throws instead of just memoizing.
findings.rationale: The declared key type is `object`, so this only bites if a cast or `any` lets a primitive through — plausible in a parser walking arbitrary input. Low confidence, but the failure mode changes from benign to a thrown exception, so it is cheap to check the call sites that write into `buckets`/`backEdges`.
